questions.question: Which Question Paper Type of Biology is given to you?
questions.explanation: This is a paper identification question. The correct answer is Type C as indicated in the paper header.

questions.question: The function of the red head in male Agama lizards is to

options.A: conceal and camouflage the animal from predators
options.B: scare other males from the territory
options.C: attract female lizards for mating purposes
options.D: warn predators of the distastefulness of the animal

questions.explanation: The bright red head of male Agama lizards is a sexual display characteristic used to attract females during mating season.

questions.question: In which of the following species is the biomass of an individual the smallest?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a microscopic algae with the smallest individual biomass compared to the other larger organisms listed.

questions.question: Seed plants are divided into
questions.explanation: Seed plants (spermatophytes) are classified into angiosperms (flowering plants) and gymnosperms (cone-bearing plants).

questions.question: In which of the following groups of vertebrates is parental care mostly exhibited?
questions.explanation: Mammals show the most extensive parental care, including gestation, nursing, and extended care of young.

questions.question: Which of the organisms represented are notable agricultural pests?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, organisms II and IV represent agricultural pests that damage crops.

questions.question: An economic importance of the organism represented by IV is that

options.A: it transmits water borne disease to humans
options.B: it is destructive to farm crops
options.D: it helps in the control of mosquito larvae

questions.explanation: Organism IV represents an agricultural pest that causes economic damage by destroying farm crops.

questions.question: The adult form of III is a vector of
questions.explanation: The adult form of organism III (likely a blackfly) is a vector for elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis).

questions.question: The adaptive importance of nuptial flight from termite colonies is to

options.A: disperse the reproductives in order to establish new colonies
options.B: provide abundant food for birds and other animals during the early rains
options.C: ensure cross-breeding between members of one colony and another
options.D: expel the reproductives so as to provide enough food for other members

questions.explanation: Nuptial flights allow reproductive termites to disperse and establish new colonies in different locations.

questions.question: The gas evolved in the process is
questions.explanation: Based on the experimental setup, carbon dioxide is the gas evolved during the process shown.

questions.question: The experimental set-up above is used to demonstrate the process of
questions.explanation: The experimental setup demonstrates fermentation, where organisms produce carbon dioxide as a byproduct.

questions.question: Which of the following can cause shrinkage of living cells?
questions.explanation: Hypertonic solutions cause water to move out of cells, leading to cell shrinkage (plasmolysis in plants).

questions.question: Which of the following is true of leucocytes?

options.B: they are most numerous and ramify all cells
options.D: they are involved in blood clotting

questions.explanation: Leucocytes (white blood cells) are large, nucleated cells involved in immune responses.

questions.question: The conversion of a nutrient into a molecule in the body of a consumer is referred to as
questions.explanation: Assimilation is the process by which absorbed nutrients are converted into body molecules.

questions.question: The ability of living organisms to detect and respond to changes in the environment is referred to as
questions.explanation: Irritability is the ability of living organisms to detect and respond to environmental stimuli.

questions.question: In mammals, the exchange of nutrients and metabolic products occurs in the
questions.explanation: The lymphatic system facilitates the exchange of nutrients and metabolic products between blood and tissues.

questions.question: An example of an endospermous seed is
questions.explanation: Maize grain is endospermous, containing endosperm tissue that provides nutrition to the developing embryo.

questions.question: Which of the above modes of nutrition is correctly matched with the organism that exhibits it?
questions.explanation: Based on the options given, option II correctly matches the nutritional mode with the appropriate organism.

questions.question: In which of the test tubes will glucose be detected after complete hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Glucose will be detected in test tubes II and III where hydrolysis can occur due to acid and enzyme respectively.

questions.question: The enzyme involved in the hydrolysis is
questions.explanation: Sucrase is the enzyme that hydrolyzes sucrose (cane sugar) into glucose and fructose.

questions.question: The part of the mammalian ear responsible for the maintenance of balance is the
questions.explanation: The semicircular canals in the inner ear (part of the cochlear complex) are responsible for balance.

questions.question: The path followed by air as it passes through the lungs in mammals is
questions.explanation: Air flows from trachea to bronchi to bronchioles and finally to alveoli where gas exchange occurs.

questions.question: The movement response of a cockroach away from a light source can be described as
questions.explanation: Movement away from light is negative phototaxis (or negative phototaxism).

questions.question: The vascular tissues in higher plants are responsible for

options.A: the movement of food and water
options.D: the transport of gases and water

questions.explanation: Vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) transport water, minerals, and food throughout the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following organs regulates the levels of water, salts, hydrogen ions and urea in the mammalian blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys regulate blood composition by filtering waste products and maintaining water and salt balance.

questions.question: The sequence of the one-way gaseous exchange mechanism in a fish is
questions.explanation: Water flows from mouth through gills (where gas exchange occurs) and exits through the operculum.

questions.question: The type of asexual reproduction that is common to both Paramecium and protists is
questions.explanation: Binary fission is the common form of asexual reproduction in Paramecium and many other protists.

questions.question: In nature, plants and animals are perpetually engaged in mutualism because

options.B: all animals rely on food produced by plants
options.C: they utilize respiratory wastes of each other

questions.explanation: Plants and animals have a mutualistic relationship where animals depend on plants for food and oxygen, while plants benefit from carbon dioxide and pollination services.

questions.question: The percentage of humus in the soil sample is
questions.explanation: Calculating from the given data: Humus = (99.0 - 95.5)/(101.5 - 80.5) × 100 = 3.5/21 × 100 = 16.7%

questions.question: An example of a filter-feeding animal is
questions.explanation: Baleen whales are filter feeders that strain small organisms from water through their baleen plates.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the population pyramid of a developing country?
questions.explanation: Developing countries typically have population pyramids with broad bases (high birth rates) and shorter lifespans.

questions.question: The interaction of a community of organisms with its abiotic environment constitutes
questions.explanation: An ecosystem consists of a community of organisms interacting with their physical environment.

questions.question: The vector of the malaria parasite is
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes are the vectors that transmit malaria parasites to humans.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used to measure relative humidity?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer is the instrument used to measure relative humidity in the air.

questions.question: Exo-erythrocytic phase of the life cycle of malaria parasite occurs in the
questions.explanation: The exo-erythrocytic phase of malaria parasite development occurs in liver cells before entering red blood cells.

questions.question: Habitats are generally classified into
questions.explanation: Habitats are broadly classified into aquatic (water-based) and terrestrial (land-based) environments.

questions.question: Dracunculiasis can be contacted through
questions.explanation: Dracunculiasis (Guinea worm disease) is contracted by drinking water contaminated with infected copepods.

questions.question: Which of the following groups of environmental factors are density-dependent?

options.A: Food, salinity, accumulation of metabolites and light
options.C: Food predation, disease and accumulation of metabolites

questions.explanation: Density-dependent factors like food availability, predation, disease, and waste accumulation vary with population density.

questions.question: Millet, sorghum, maize and onions are common crops grown in Nigeria in the
questions.explanation: These crops are commonly grown in the Sudan savanna region of Nigeria due to suitable climate conditions.

questions.question: In which of the following biomes is the south western part of Nigeria located?
questions.explanation: Southwestern Nigeria is located in the tropical rainforest biome characterized by high rainfall and dense vegetation.

questions.question: The inheritable characters that are determined by a gene located on the X-chromosome is
questions.explanation: Traits controlled by genes on the X-chromosome are called sex-linked traits.

questions.question: Lack of space in a population could lead to an increase in
questions.explanation: Overcrowding due to lack of space increases competition and stress, leading to higher disease rates.

questions.question: If the cross of a red-flowered plant with a white-flowered plant produces a pink-flowered plant, it is an example of
questions.explanation: When neither allele is completely dominant, resulting in a blended phenotype, it demonstrates incomplete dominance.

questions.question: Which of the following theories was NOT considered by Darwin in his evolutionary theory?
questions.explanation: Use and disuse was part of Lamarck's theory, not Darwin's. Darwin focused on variation, natural selection, and survival of the fittest.

questions.question: The crossing of individuals of the same species with different genetic characters is
questions.explanation: Cross breeding involves mating individuals of the same species with different genetic characteristics.

questions.question: The number of alleles controlling blood groups in humans
questions.explanation: Human ABO blood groups are controlled by three alleles: IA, IB, and i.

questions.question: During blood transfusion, agglutination may occur as a result of the reaction between
questions.explanation: Agglutination occurs when incompatible antigens on donor red blood cells react with corresponding antibodies in recipient plasma.

questions.question: The fallacy in Lamarck's evolutionary theory was the assumption that

options.A: traits are acquired through disuse of body parts
options.D: traits are acquired through the use of body parts

questions.explanation: Lamarck incorrectly assumed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime could be inherited by offspring.

questions.question: The bright coloured eye spots on the wings of moths are an example of
questions.explanation: Eye spots on moth wings are examples of mimicry, resembling the eyes of larger predators to deter attackers.

questions.question: The wings of a bat and those of a bird are examples of
questions.explanation: Bat wings and bird wings are examples of convergent evolution - similar structures that evolved independently for flight.
